name: Crownhold
desc: A giant concentric castle on the crag: two rings of walls, 24 towers, 46 m keep.

name: The Crown Tower
desc: The 46 m great keep, seven storeys, seat of the Crown.

name: Great Hall of the Kings
desc: Where the court feasts and the king hears petitions.

name: The Crowning Stone
desc: A prehistoric stone carried up from the henge: every monarch is crowned on it.

name: King's Gate
desc: Great gatehouse with twin 30 m drum towers and a walled barbican.

name: City wall & seven gates
desc: 46 towers, seven gatehouses and two water gates where the River Wend passes under chains.

name: The Hallowstones
desc: A 420 m henge, 4,000 years older than the city: ditch, bank and 150 standing stones.

name: The Cove
desc: Three giant stones at the heart of the North Circle; oaths are sworn here.

name: The Obelisk
desc: The tallest stone of the South Circle, the city's midsummer sundial.

name: The Serpent Avenue
desc: Two rows of stones winding 600 m from the henge to the river.

name: Wardenhouse - YOUR HOUSE
desc: Home of The Warden of the Stones, keeper of the ancient stones. Start here.

name: The Giant's Barrow
desc: A 120 m chambered long barrow, the tomb of the 'giant' the city's tales remember.

name: The Druids' Row
desc: Thirteen stones in a dead-straight line pointing at the midwinter sunrise.

name: The Three Kings' Table
desc: A portal tomb on the Minster lawn; three kings' bones are said to lie beneath.

name: The Field of Mounds
desc: Seven Bronze Age burial mounds kept as a public meadow.

name: The Grand Market
desc: A 260 x 120 m square with 150 stalls, fountains and the Needle at its heart.

name: The Needle
desc: A 9 m prehistoric menhir left standing in the market: deals are sealed by touching it.

name: The Cloth Hall & Belfry
desc: Vast cloth market with an 84 m belfry, the tallest tower in the city.

name: The Great Guildhall
desc: Seat of the city council and the twelve great guilds.

name: The King's Column
desc: A 32 m column topped by the first king, facing the stones he swore to protect.

name: Haymarket
desc: Carters and hay wains from the northern farms.

name: Fish Market
desc: Fresh catch straight off the boats at King's Quay.

name: Corn Market
desc: Grain market on the south bank, by the Old Bridge.

name: The Old Bridge
desc: A 150 m stone bridge of 19 arches carrying 28 shops and houses and a chapel.

name: Mill Bridge
desc: Seven arches with three corn mills hung off its side.

name: King's Quay
desc: Warehouses, treadwheel cranes and sea-going cogs on the River Wend.

name: Stonehallow Minster
desc: Gothic cathedral 200 m long; its spire reaches 120 m, the tallest thing in the realm.

name: The Queen's Maze
desc: A 60 m hedge maze; at its heart a sundial stone.

name: The Queen's Gardens
desc: Royal pleasure gardens: parterres, ponds, lime avenues and the summer palace.

name: King's Park
desc: Ancient woodland kept wild inside the walls, with deer, a mere and the barrow.

name: Collegium of the Seven Stars
desc: Two colleges, a great library and the Physic Garden of healing herbs.

name: Hospital of St. Brigid
desc: Infirmary, almshouse and herb garden run by the Brigidine sisters.

name: Whitecross Abbey
desc: Benedictine abbey whose monks first wrote down the legends of the stones.

name: Greyfriars
desc: A friary of preaching brothers.

name: Blackfriars
desc: A friary of preaching brothers.

name: Cattle Fair
desc: Livestock fair outside the gate every Thursday.

name: Horse Fair
desc: Livestock fair outside the gate every Thursday.
